lanes.text: This is last-missing for fpbs-locally-free-groups-have-fixed-price: closing it gives fixed price for every locally free group.

Thompson's group F has no live route tree in the graph. Build one: a decomposition of amenability of F (or of its negation) into prerequisites that can each fail on their own, written as new OPEN claims plus a route, each prerequisite stated precisely and connected to known literature (Moore's Folner function bounds, Kaimanovich's non-Liouville result for F, extensive amenability, Juschenko-Monod). Then attack the most promising prerequisite in full.

Attack the negation: that F is NOT amenable. Find the strongest precise sufficient condition (spectral gap of a specific Markov operator, a paradoxical decomposition via the action on dyadic rationals, a cost or l2-invariant, a uniform lower bound on cogrowth) and either prove it or prove exactly where every member of that class dies. Record the obstruction as a claim.

Paradigm lane: amenability via extensive amenability and amenable actions (Juschenko-Monod, Juschenko-Nekrashevych-de la Salle). State precisely which action of F with amenable stabilizers and which recurrence/extensive-amenability property would suffice, and either prove it or kill the approach class with a precise invariant.

Computation lane under experiments/thompson-f-2026-09-17/: compute rigorous bounds (isoperimetric profile of explicit finite sets, return probabilities, cogrowth series coefficients) in the standard generators of F and say what they change: either a counterexample to a proposed approach or quantitative data that kills a whole class of Folner-set constructions. Keep scripts cheap and reproducible.

Paradigm lane: known consequences of amenability that F would need (Liouville-type, entropy, invariant means on the Thompson-like groupoid, the Tamari/associahedra graphs). Find one known-open equivalent or sufficient reformulation that is sharp, and prove a nontrivial step of it or show exactly why it is as hard as the original.

No route tree yet for Haagerup property of nV. Build one: Farley showed V acts properly on a CAT(0) cube complex; state precisely what breaks for 2V and decompose Haagerup for nV into prerequisites (proper wall structure, proper conditionally negative definite function), then attack the most promising one.

Attack the negation for nV, n >= 2: search for relative property (T) pairs or infinite Kazhdan subgroups (or a proof that every Kazhdan subgroup is finite). Record either a construction or a precise obstruction class claim.

Decomposition lane: reduce Haagerup of nV to statements about germ groupoids or finite pieces (e.g. a-T-menability of the groupoid of germs, proper actions on spaces with measured walls built from dyadic bricks) so each prerequisite can fail on its own. Write the route and push the first step.

Counterexample direction: look for a finitely generated group with solvable word problem that cannot embed in any finitely presented simple group. Name the invariant that every finitely presented simple overgroup would force (decidability of some property, growth of Dehn function relative to word problem, finiteness of some cohomological type) and either produce the group or kill the invariant class precisely.

Build a NEW decomposition of Boone-Higman not through decidable-edge HNN extensions: e.g. via embedding into twisted Brin-Thompson groups or Rover-Nekrashevych groups of computable self-similar actions, stated as prerequisites that each can fail. Check bin/cairn search first to avoid duplicating existing routes.

Counterexample direction: a non-surjunctive group. Name the class of candidate groups (non-sofic candidates, Kazhdan groups with strong rigidity, groups of intermediate structure) and the precise mechanism a strict injective non-surjective cellular automaton would need; either produce a construction step or kill the whole class with the invariant where it dies.

Build a NEW decomposition of Gottschalk surjunctivity beyond sofic groups that is not already in the graph (check bin/cairn search): e.g. via local embeddings into a class closed under the needed operations, weak sofic approximations with entropy, or Rokhlin entropy. State each prerequisite precisely so it can fail on its own, write the route, and attack the first step.

Paradigm lane: route from the proven 2-to-2 games theorem (Khot-Minzer-Safra) toward UGC with imperfect completeness. Decompose into precise prerequisites (a Grassmann-type test with low soundness for unique constraints, a structure theorem for small-set expanders of a specific graph family) and push the first genuinely open one.

Counter-direction: kill a whole class of hardness reductions with a precise algorithm, e.g. show sum-of-squares of a fixed degree solves every instance produced by a named family of reductions, naming the step where each member of the family fails. Record it as an obstruction claim.

New decomposition toward an explicit non-hyperlinear group using MIP* = RE (Ji-Natarajan-Vidick-Wright-Yuen): from a non-local game with no finite-dimensional near-optimal strategies, build a finitely presented group whose hyperlinearity would imply the game's value is approximable. State prerequisites precisely (which group, which trace inequality) and attack the first step. Check bin/cairn search for existing routes first.

Counterexample direction: a countable group without fixed price. Name the candidate classes (groups with infinite ell2 Betti numbers varying, groups like SL3(Z) x free, Tarski monsters) and the invariant that would force two free actions of different cost; either build it or kill the class precisely.

Decomposition via weak containment: Bernoulli shifts are weakly contained in every free action (Abert-Weiss), and cost is upper semicontinuous under weak containment (Kechris). Fixed price is then equivalent to a precise lower-semicontinuity statement. Write that decomposition as claims and routes if not already present (bin/cairn search), and attack the lower-semicontinuity statement on the widest class you can.

New decomposition of pc < pu for every nonamenable Cayley graph (Benjamini-Schramm conjecture) using Hutchcroft's supercritical sharpness and ell2 methods: state prerequisites that each can fail, check bin/cairn search for existing routes, write the route and attack the first open step.

Counterexample direction for pc < pu: name the class of nonamenable Cayley graphs where the gap could close (Grigorchuk-type nonamenable groups with amenable-like local structure, products with amenable factors with large generating sets) and the invariant that would force pc = pu; either construct or kill the class with a precise obstruction.
